details:
Project Details — AstroPaint

AstroPaint is an interactive educational website designed to make Mars exploration more engaging and accessible for children and young space enthusiasts. It combines creativity, coloring, and space science to help users discover NASA's Mars rovers and understand the technology behind their missions.

The website allows users to explore Mars rover illustrations, color different parts of the rovers, and interact with individual components to learn about their functions. Instead of learning through text alone, users can actively engage with the machines that have helped humanity explore the Red Planet.

AstroPaint connects with the NASA Space Apps challenge, "Abandoned but not Forgotten," by introducing younger audiences to Mars exploration technology and the robotic explorers associated with missions that leave equipment behind on the Martian surface. It provides a creative starting point for understanding these machines and their role in space exploration, with opportunities to expand into dedicated interactive stories about abandoned mission equipment.

The main benefit of AstroPaint is that it makes complex space-related topics easier and more enjoyable to understand. By combining visual learning with hands-on interaction, it encourages curiosity, creativity, and interest in science and technology. Our intended impact is to inspire children to learn more about space exploration and develop an early interest in STEM subjects.

The project was developed as a web-based interactive experience and deployed using Vercel. Google Gemini was used to generate some video content for the project. The website brings together digital illustrations, interactive coloring, and educational information in a child-friendly experience.

What makes AstroPaint creative is its approach to space education: it transforms learning about Mars rovers into an activity where children can explore, experiment with colors, and discover how different rover components work. During development, we considered accessibility for younger audiences, ease of use, educational value, visual appeal, and the importance of connecting the experience to real NASA exploration missions.

Our vision is to expand AstroPaint with more Mars missions, additional exploration equipment, and interactive stories about the objects left behind on other worlds.
